text: Keep watching. As the two sides even out, the counts come closer, until the concentrations are equal and the two numbers run level. The particles have not stopped: they still move and still cross both ways, but there is no net movement now, so the arrow fades. And notice what drove all of this: the particles' own kinetic energy, and no ATP from a cell. That is what passive means. It matters because cells exchange substances with their surroundings all the time, and passive routes let them do a lot of it without spending ATP. The membrane decides which substance takes which route.
